newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Sterling boosts cash cocoa demand but supply tight.
newsitem.headline: Sterling boosts cash cocoa demand but supply tight.

text.p: Cash cocoa buyers in Europe have taken advantage of sterling's drop against European currencies this week but dwindling supplies from major origins such as the Ivory Coast have kept business at a minimum, traders said.

Cocoa futures have firmed this week, with the benchmark July contract trading up around 1,015 stg a tonne against 990 stg a week ago, but a post-election slide in the pound has offered industry buyers some compensation.
"The net effect has been that prices have stayed relatively stable and it's been enough to attract a bit of buying," one trader said, adding the quantities were small.
Holidays across much of Europe on Thursday meant many players had also taken Friday off, accentuating the quiet tone.
The lack of volume on the terminal market in London reflected the slack cash business in continental Europe.

Traders said the Ivory Coast and Ghana had been selling cocoa into the European market earlier this week but quality problems on Ivorian cocoa were lingering. Much of the cocoa not already shipped was being classed as defective.
"There's not much coming out (of Abidjan) and whatever is left is not up to standard," another trader said.
European differentials were quoted as steady on last week's levels with Ivory Coast beans trading at 25 to 30 stg under the terminal market and Ghana at between five and 15 stg under.
On the demand side, traders noted some industry buying for the second half of the year and into 1998 but the hand-to-mouth philosophy of many consumers was still holding sway, they added.

A further depreciation in sterling would encourage more demand, they conceded, and this could be helped by a lower terminal market, should recent bearish crop estimates turn out to be true. --Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
